FOURTH MEASURED INSTANCE OF THE STALE SHARED DAEMON, AND THE SECOND THAT COST FIVE MERGED PRs — with the remedy already shipped both times.

2026-08-08 (instance three, recorded in tests/the_server_says_when_it_is_stale.rs): "Anthony restarted the session specifically to pick up a new binary, and the served surface did not move — `--shared` is a CLIENT that re-attaches to the detached daemon. Five merged PRs had been built, gated and shipped without one of them ever running live."

2026-08-19, MOVE FOR MOVE THE SAME: PRs #254 #255 #256 #257 #258 merged, all green. Anthony restarted the session deliberately to pick up the new binary. NOTHING MOVED. Measured at the process table: pid 3861122 `--serve-shared`, started 17:22:52, up 4h49m; the session's own client pid started 22:11 and re-attached to it. The binary ON DISK was current — stamp matched the source hash and contained `level_spine_disagreement` five times — while the process answering every call was four hours older than the code.

⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN JUST FIXING: the detection existed. `served_by.stale` was built after instance three, is tested, and says in its own note "A SESSION RESTART ALONE, WITHOUT `--stop-shared`, CHANGES NOTHING". It rides on `graph_report`. Over roughly two hundred tool calls that day the session called `loop_status` eight times and `graph_report` ZERO — while the session-start hook says "loop_status is the one cheap call" and the stop hook nudges to the same place. The remedy was one call away and in the wrong room.

📌 SAME SHAPE AS TWO OTHER FINDINGS THE SAME DAY, which is why it is filed as a pattern and not an incident: `ruling: parks` (documented on the tool, absent from the defect the reader is looking at) and `Component.level` (indexed and populated, with no way to ask by it). Typed mechanism present, instruction absent from the place of use, every time.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any other computed surface silently depends on binary currency the same way. Only `graph_report` and `loop_status` were examined.
